reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR updates the Internet-Draft text for the Credential Presentation → OIDC Claims bridge (adding/reshaping RP requirements and credential metadata) and adds local development conveniences (devcontainer + simple HTTP server script). **Changes:** - Adds a `serve.sh` helper to start/stop a local HTTP server and ignores its PID file. - Adds a devcontainer configuration intended to set up Python + Ruby tooling for building the draft. - Expands and restructures draft text (RP requirements section, credential entry fields, trust lists, freshness requirement, and a holder-binding registry). ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | serve.sh | Adds a start/stop wrapper for `python3 -m http.server` with PID tracking. | | .gitignore | Ignores the `.serve.pid` file created by `serve.sh`. | | .devcontainer/devcontainer.json | Introduces a devcontainer setup for draft development. | | .devcontainer/devcontainer-lock.json | Locks the devcontainer Ruby feature to a resolved digest/version. | | draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md | Adds/updates specification text for RP requests, credential entry metadata, trust list handling, and registries. |
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

comments.body: `python3 -m http.server` binds to all interfaces by default, but the script prints a localhost-only URL. This can unintentionally expose the draft over the network (e.g., in a devcontainer) and the message is misleading. Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1 and keep the output consistent.

The `stop` path removes the PID file even if `kill` fails for reasons other than "not running" (e.g., permission errors), which can leave the server running but make it impossible to stop via this script. Capture the PID, check whether it's running, and only remove the PID file after a successful stop or confirmed absence.

`postCreateCommand` runs `pip install -r lib/requirements.txt`, but this repo doesn't have a `lib/` directory until the i-d-template is cloned (via the Makefile rule for `lib/main.mk`). As written, devcontainer creation will fail on a fresh checkout. Initialize the template first before installing requirements.

`valid_until` says the OP may include expired credentials if the RP "explicitly indicates willingness to accept expired credentials", but the document doesn't define any request signal/parameter for that. Either define such a parameter in the RP request structure, or remove the exception to avoid an unimplementable requirement.

## Pull request overview

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (4)</summary>

**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:161**
* This section says the RP MUST include credential type scopes, but later the spec says a request for credentials can be made via the "requested_credentials" claims parameter or a registered scope. As written, it's unclear whether scopes are mandatory or whether `requested_credentials.credential_sets` alone is sufficient to request credential types. Please align the RP requirements text with the rest of the document by allowing either mechanism (scopes and/or credential_sets).
```
An RP that wishes to receive credential data via this bridge MUST
include the appropriate credential type scopes in the OIDC
Authentication Request.  Each scope corresponds to a credential type
(e.g., "ehic", "pda1").  The presence of any credential type scope
signals to the OP that the "requested_credentials" claim parameter
```
**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:190**
* The "value" constraint text says the OP "MUST reject the credential" if the value doesn't match. Elsewhere (Credential Mapping) the document describes this as the credential "not satisfying the request", which is more precise (especially when there are alternative credential sets or multiple credentials of the same type). Consider using the same phrasing here for consistency.
```
   value
   : A JSON value that the disclosed claim MUST exactly equal.
     If present, the OP MUST verify that the disclosed claim value
     matches and MUST reject the credential if it does not.
     If omitted, any disclosed value is accepted.
```
**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:669**
* In the Credential Entry Object definition, the OP MUST set `type` based on the presented credential. Here, the text says the OP MUST use the mapped "type" value when constructing Credential Entry objects, which could be read as overriding the credential-derived value. It would be clearer to say the mapping is used to translate scope -> wallet query, and that the returned Credential Entry `type` is populated from the credential (and should match the mapping).
```
and the "type" value that will appear in the corresponding Credential
Entry.  The OP MUST use the "type" value from this mapping when
constructing Credential Entry objects, enabling the OP to translate
the RP's scope request into the correct credential query (e.g., a
DCQL query with the appropriate "vct_values" or "doctype_value")
```
**serve.sh:13**
* The script writes the PID file and prints a success message immediately after starting the server in the background. If `python3 -m http.server` fails to bind (e.g., port already in use) the process may exit right away, leaving a stale PID file and a misleading "Serving on..." message. Capture `$!`, verify the process is still alive before writing the PID file, and fail fast on startup errors.
```
    python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 "$PORT" &
    echo $! > "$PIDFILE"
    echo "Serving on http://localhost:$PORT (pid $!)"
```
</details>

## Pull request overview

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (4)</summary>

**serve.sh:27**
* `kill -0 "$pid"` / `kill "$pid"` should use `--` (to prevent option parsing) and should avoid killing an unrelated process if the PID file is stale/reused. Validate the PID is numeric and confirm it’s the expected http.server process before sending the signal.
```
      pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
      if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Not running (stale PID file)"
        rm -f "$PIDFILE"
      elif kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
```
**serve.sh:2**
* For consistency with the repo’s other shell script(s) and to avoid silent failures, enable strict bash mode (e.g., `set -euo pipefail`) near the top of this script (see tag-release.sh:2).
```
#!/bin/bash
PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
```
**serve.sh:10**
* The PID-file check can be tricked into calling `kill` with an option-like PID (e.g., a PID file containing "-TERM"), and it can also treat an unrelated process with a reused PID as “already running”. Read/validate the PID and verify it matches the expected http.server command before exiting.

This issue also appears on line 23 of the same file.
```
  start)
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDFILE")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Already running on port $PORT (pid $(cat "$PIDFILE"))"
      exit 1
    fi
```
**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:1172**
* This bullet mixes SHOULD and MUST in a way that becomes non-implementable: if maintaining an allowlist is only SHOULD, you can’t also require rejecting URIs not on that allowlist. Consider making the allowlist requirement a MUST (since rejection implies one exists).
```
*  The OP SHOULD maintain an allowlist of permitted trust list URIs
   and MUST reject URIs not on that list.  This prevents an RP from
   directing the OP to fetch arbitrary resources (SSRF).
```
</details>

## Pull request overview

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (5)</summary>

**serve.sh:28**
* `stop` trusts the PID file blindly and may send SIGTERM to an unrelated process if the PID has been reused or the PID file was tampered with. It should validate the PID file contents and ensure the PID still refers to the expected `python3 -m http.server` process before killing it.
```
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
      pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
      if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Not running (stale PID file)"
        rm -f "$PIDFILE"
      elif kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Stopped (pid $pid)"
```
**serve.sh:2**
* This script doesn’t enable Bash strict mode, unlike the existing tag-release.sh. Without `set -euo pipefail`, failures (e.g., failed `cat`, unset vars) can be silently ignored and lead to confusing behavior.
```
#!/bin/bash
PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
```
**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:130**
* The ASCII architecture diagram is currently malformed (missing/shifted column separators and a truncated "+----------+" line), which breaks rendering and makes the flow hard to read. Restoring consistent box borders/spacing fixes the diagram.
```
+--------+              +------------------+            +----------+
|        | 1. OIDC AuthN  |        OP        | 2. Present  |          |
|   RP   | -------------> |     (Bridge)     | ----------> |  Wallet  |
|        |              |                | <---------- |          |
|        |              |                | 3. Response |          |
|        |              |                |           +----------+
```
**.devcontainer/devcontainer.json:7**
* Using the `pip` shim directly can install into an unexpected interpreter environment (or fail if `pip` isn’t on PATH). Using `python3 -m pip` ensures the packages are installed for the devcontainer’s Python image.
```
  "postCreateCommand": "make lib/main.mk && pip install -r lib/requirements.txt && gem install kramdown-rfc",
```
**serve.sh:10**
* `start` treats any live PID in .serve.pid as “already running”. If the PID has been reused by an unrelated process, `start` will refuse to start the server until the PID file is manually removed. Verifying the PID refers to the expected `python3 -m http.server` process (and otherwise treating it as stale) avoids false positives.

This issue also appears on line 22 of the same file.
```
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDFILE")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Already running on port $PORT (pid $(cat "$PIDFILE"))"
      exit 1
    fi
```
</details>

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (3)</summary>

**serve.sh:24**
* `stop` uses the PID from $PIDFILE without validating it. As with `start`, an unexpected value (e.g., `-1`) can cause `kill` to signal an unintended set of processes. Add a numeric PID check and treat invalid contents as a stale PID file.
```
      pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
      if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
```
**draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md:791**
* This sentence says a credential request can be indicated by the `requested_credential_sets` claims parameter *or* a registered scope, but the RP Requirements section states scopes are always required. This is internally inconsistent; either scopes are mandatory or the OP needs a path that works without them.
```
When the OP receives an OIDC Authentication Request that includes a
request for credentials (via the "requested_credential_sets" claims
parameter or a registered scope), it MUST:
```
**serve.sh:3**
* PIDFILE is relative to the current working directory, so `start` and `stop` will look at different PID files if the script is invoked from different directories (and may leave orphaned servers). Prefer anchoring the PID file to the script directory (while still allowing an override via $PIDFILE).
```
PIDFILE=".serve.pid"
```
</details>

comments.body:
The PID read from $PIDFILE is used directly in `kill`. If the PID file is corrupted (e.g., contains a negative number like `-1`), `kill` can target a process group or all processes the user can signal. Validate the PID is a positive integer before using it.

This issue also appears on line 23 of the same file.

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR updates the OIDC Credential Bridge draft to replace the prior claims-based request mechanism with an optional DCQL-based mode while tightening the response/verification contract (including critical verification signals), and adds a markdownlint configuration to support editorial formatting. **Changes:** - Define two request modes: scope-based (required) and DCQL-based (optional), including discovery signaling via `dcql_query_supported`. - Update the `presented_credentials`/Credential Set and Credential Entry model (e.g., `type` becomes an array; add reserved Credential Set `id`; extend `verification` with `crit`, `trust_status`, and `protected_headers`). - Add an OpenID4VP/DCQL binding appendix and a placeholder DIDComm binding appendix; add a markdownlint configuration file. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | draft-svensson-credential-oidc-bridge.md | Reworks request/response semantics to introduce DCQL mode, expands verification/trust signaling, and adds protocol binding appendices. | | .markdownlint.json | Adds markdownlint rule configuration for consistent document linting. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

comments.body: The document now models value constraints in DCQL using the "values" array, but this consumer guidance still refers to a "value" constraint and implies exact equality to a single value. This is inconsistent with the DCQL profile described earlier.

The semantics for "trust_status" say that when it is absent the RP must assume the OP did not perform a trust-status check, but the registry's "unknown" value also includes "no trust-status check". This overlaps/conflicts and makes it unclear when an OP should omit the member vs include "unknown".

The reserved top-level member name "id" in a Credential Set can collide with a credential key (scope value / DCQL Credential Query id). The current text only constrains RPs, but in practice the OP also needs to ensure "id" is never used as a key in "credential_presentations_supported" (and therefore never as a scope value), otherwise the response structure becomes ambiguous.
